  Get IRT results without learning R first: Point and click in the
  workbench, describe the analysis in words, or share a dashboard.

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

You do not need to know R to use mirtverse. You need to install it once and
type one line; after that, you can work with buttons or plain language.

## Try it before you install anything

[Open the live example dashboard](../dashboard/sat12-demo.html). It shows the
results for a 32-item test: Which items work, which need review, and how
scores are distributed. It runs in your browser, and you can make one like it
for your own test.

## Your path in three steps

**1. Install R, RStudio and mirtverse (once, about 10 minutes).**

- Install R from [CRAN](https://cloud.r-project.org/) and
  [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/), both free.
- Open RStudio and paste this line into the Console (bottom left), then
  press Enter:

```r
install.packages("mirtverse", repos = c("https://okanbulut.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

**2. Open the workbench.** Paste these two lines:

```r
library(mirtverse)
launch_workbench()
```

A window opens with eight steps: Load your data (CSV, Excel, SPSS), choose a
model, check items, score people and download a report. The
[workbench guide](../articles/workbench.html) walks through each step.

**3. Or describe what you want in words.** `mv_ask()` writes the analysis for
you, and you can read it before it runs:

```r
mv_ask("fit a Rasch model, check item fit and make a report", data = mydata)
```

It works offline for common analyses; see the [guide](mv-ask-guide.html).

## Coming from other software?

- **Winsteps or other Rasch software:** The workbench fits the Rasch model,
  item fit and a Wright map, and writes the R code so you can see the
  equivalent of each step.
- **SPSS or Excel:** Load your `.sav`, `.xlsx` or `.csv` file directly in the
  workbench.
- **ltm, eRm, TAM or irtQ in R:** `mirtify()` translates your code; see
  [Moving to mirt](mirtify.html).

## Words you will see

The [glossary](glossary.html) explains each term (discrimination,
information, DIF and so on) in plain language.
